oncall-bot: ALERT: Config rule triggered: SecurityGroup sg-03f4a9c2 attached to `prod-db` has ingress 0.0.0.0/0 on TCP/22 (detected 2025-11-15T14:22:48Z)
maya: saw this, assigning. triaging now — marking P0 for potential exposure of DB host access.
alex: can you paste `describe-security-groups` output? want to confirm exact rule and which instance it's attached to.
maya: output below:
```
> aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-03f4a9c2
{\n  "SecurityGroups": [\n    {\n      "GroupId": "sg-03f4a9c2",\n      "GroupName": "prod-db-sg",\n      "IpPermissions": [\n        {\n          "IpProtocol": "tcp",\n          "FromPort": 22,\n          "ToPort": 22,\n          "IpRanges": [ { "CidrIp": "0.0.0.0/0" } ]\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```
sam: taking immediate action — revoking the wide-open rule and restricting to internal ops CIDR. executing now:
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-03f4a9c2 --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-03f4a9c2 --protocol tcp --port 22 --cidr 10.0.0.0/8
```
oncall-bot: CHANGE: eg-2025-11-15-01 applied by sam@infra (patch) — revoke + authorize completed at 2025-11-15T14:27:03Z.
jordan: I'll validate connectivity for ops jumpbox and monitoring probes. running quick SSH test to internal IP...
jordan: success, ops can still reach hosts via jumpbox. monitoring rechecks passing.
nisha: sec-eng: good containment. next: we need attribution and scope. check CloudTrail for who called `AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress` and whether this was an automated change from CI. also check for any suspicious logins around 14:20 UTC.
maya: CloudTrail lookup shows an `AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress` event at 2025-11-15T14:20:51Z performed by IAM role `infra-deployer@redwood-ci` from IP 35.200.77.12. It appears to have been created during a deploy step.
alex: so the deploy pipeline has permission to change SGs — that's a policy failure. immediate actions: remove ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress from `infra-deployer` role, restrict to tagged resources via condition `aws:ResourceTag/managed-by: terraform` and open PR to infra repo.
sam: creating emergency PR now to lock down role and add a terraform plan guard to prevent 0.0.0.0/0 for prod SGs. also rotating deployer service account credentials and revoking any short-lived tokens issued in the last 1h.
jordan: will also scan CloudTrail for `ConsoleLogin` and `AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress` in the 1h window, plus check DB auth logs for direct/root attempts. preliminary scan shows no abnormal DB auths.
nisha: checklist for post-incident: 1) Confirm no compromised keys / data exfil (CloudTrail + DB logs) 2) Add IAM guard (deny policy) and enforce via policy-as-code 3) Add alert rule for any SG with 0.0.0.0/0 in prod 4) Update runbook + incident ticket + schedule postmortem. assign owners: infra-sre (sam, jordan), sec-eng (nisha), devex (alex) for policy PR.
maya: created ticket INC-2025-789: "Prod SG opened to 0.0.0.0/0 during deploy — mitigate + RBAC fix" with initial notes and actions. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2025-789
sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3421 (emergency: restrict infra-deployer IAM + add terraform check). also adding pre-commit hook that fails plan with open cidr in prod.
alex: we'll also add a CloudWatch metric filter -> PagerDuty for open SGs in prod, and a Config rule remediation runbook. nisha please own postmortem and exec summary for leadership.
nisha: will run postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PT, include root cause, timeline, remediation (IAM policy change + runbook + KMS/audit checks). note: check KMS key access logs for any anomalies — if any DB snapshots were taken recently, we should verify snapshot encryption keys and rotation.
maya: for now state = mitigated. no evidence of credentials exfil or DB access. ticket updated with timeline and artifacts.
jordan: leaving notes for follow-up: - add nightly scan job to detect public SGs across accounts - add terraform sentinel check for prod envs - include this scenario in on-call runbook exercises.
maya: closing thread after infra PR merges and monitoring confirms no further regressions. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2025-789 logged as mitigated at 2025-11-15T14:40:40Z. Runbook updated: https://wiki.redwood.com/security/incidents/INC-2025-789
